newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CONGO NEIGHBOURS INVOLVED IN MASSACRES - BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: CONGO NEIGHBOURS INVOLVED IN MASSACRES - BELGIUM.

text.p: Belgium's secretary of state for development aid Reginald Moreels was quoted on Tuesday as saying the neighbours of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire, might be partly to blame for massacres of refugees.
"I think it is becoming more and more clear that neighbouring countries, and especially Rwanda, cannot be blameless in this," Moreels told Belgium's Humo magazine in an interview.
He said he would visit Rwanda in the near future to discuss the issue "in all openness".
Moreels denied earlier reports that he had said that the new Congo's President Laurent Kabila was responsible for a genocide.

"I only talked about the heavy violations of human righs in East Zaire and I expressed my concern about the fate of thousands of refugees who had no place to go to and officially disappeared from this planet," he told Humo.
"But I have never accused Kabila of genocide."
Humo noted that Moreels' planned four-day trip to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which was due to start on June 17, had been cancelled by Kabila but Moreels said he took it lightly.
"Congolese authorities have stressed through all possible channels that I'm still welcome," he said.
